_comment: The two great routes of the Levant. Lines are schematic corridors, not exact roads. Visible across the whole period; they explain why the north was rich and why every empire marched here.

properties.name: The Via Maris
properties.label: Via Maris — the Way of the Sea

popup.bible: The highway of the prophets' armies — 'the way of the sea' of Isaiah 9:1, along which Assyria marched.
popup.archaeology: The coastal trunk road from Egypt through Gaza, Aphek, Megiddo, and Hazor to Damascus: the economic spine of the region, and the route every empire took. Controlling it meant controlling the trade.

popup.bible: The road Moses asks Edom's king for (Num 20:17) — the Transjordanian trade route.
popup.archaeology: The inland route from the Red Sea up through Edom, Moab, Ammon, and Damascus: spice, copper, and incense traffic that made the small Transjordanian kingdoms richer than their size.
